body.statement: If exact aggregate support equality is replaced by the standard bounded-range condition \(Y_a\in[\ell_a,u_a]\), every nonempty branch contributes its full attained interval regardless of \(\tau_{a,b}^r(P)\). If the score restrictions are also removed, the branch polytope is the full box and the resulting arm endpoints are the classical Manski worst-case bounds.
body.justification: The reduction verifies that the support filter, rather than bounded outcomes alone, causes branch pruning.
body.gap: This is a required sanity reduction, not a novelty claim.
body.consumer: Readers can distinguish the exact-support contribution from standard worst-case bounded-outcome identification.
body.proof_tex:
Replace exact aggregate support equality by only \(Y_a\in[\ell_a,u_a]\).  The converse construction in \(\text{lem:branch-reduction}\) then realizes every \(x_a\in\mathcal F_{a,b}^r(P)\), including a singleton box vertex.  Since a nonempty branch polytope is compact and convex, its linear arm-mean image is the full attained interval
\[
 [L_{a,b}^r(P),U_{a,b}^r(P)],
\]
with no condition involving \(\tau_{a,b}^r(P)\).  This proves the first assertion and isolates exact aggregate support, rather than boundedness, as the source of branch pruning.

If the score restrictions are also removed, the defining inequalities disappear and
\[
 \mathcal F_{a,b}^r(P)=\prod_{j\in\mathcal M_a}[\ell_a,u_a].
\]
Because every \(p_j>0\), coordinatewise minimization and maximization yield
\[
 L_a=c_a+\ell_a\sum_{j\in\mathcal M_a}p_j,qquad
 U_a=c_a+u_a\sum_{j\in\mathcal M_a}p_j.                                       \tag{44}
\]
Consistency fixes the factual contribution \(c_a\), while the missing conditional means can independently attain every value in their support interval.  Thus (44) is both an outer bound and attainable, and it is exactly the classical bounded-outcome worst-case completion associated with \cite{Manski1990}.
